title: Oreimo
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: High-schooler Kyosuke Kosaka discovers that his fourteen-year-old sister Kirino, a popular model student who has ignored him for years, secretly collects otaku anime and adult games about 'little sisters', and she makes him her confidant. The story follows him helping her keep the hobby despite their anti-otaku policeman father. A four-volume manga adaptation of a light novel.
life_message: A good life means accepting family members' secret passions and rebuilding a sibling bond, on terms the story leaves uncomfortable.

content.note: Fan-service panty and cleavage shots of the 14-year-old sister and 'implications of incest' between siblings (Publishers Weekly); AniList and MangaUpdates tag incest, ecchi and sexual innuendo. Non-graphic; clinical description.
A 14-year-old owns adult games (AniList synopsis); PW says readers may be encouraged to indulge 'little sister' fantasies.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Kirino guards her reputation; the father's disapproval is answered with secrecy, not confrontation (AniList).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Kirino pursues her hobby against the family rule (AniList).

Civic vs kin.evidence: The story centers on the sibling bond and the family home.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Policeman father holds authority the children work around (AniList).

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Freedom to enjoy chosen hobbies is the theme.

folkways.japan: Social stigma against otaku hobbies and the importance of keeping face at school reflect Japanese norms, shown as context.

delivery.evidence: Publishers Weekly calls the contrast between brother and sister heavy-handed in characterization, not as a sermon (to verify).
delivery.note: Acceptance of the hobby is carried by the siblings' choices rather than stated lessons.

winners_losers: Kirino's hobby and the siblings' bond win; the father's anti-otaku view is the obstacle; reviewers note the framing invites fantasies about the younger sister.
to_verify: Only one review (Publishers Weekly, vol. 1); father's role from AniList synopsis
